test_title: PYST 36 - SSC CHSL 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 26 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A and B can complete a work in 12 days, B and C can complete the same work in 15 days. A, B, and C together can complete the work in 10 days. How long will it take for A and C together to complete the work?
solution:
**Given:**

A + B = 12 days

B + C = 15 days

A + B + C = 10 days

**Formula used:**

Work = LCM of days

Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

LCM of 12, 15, 10 = 60

⇒ Total work = 60 units

⇒ (A + B) 1 day work = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 units

⇒ (B + C) 1 day work = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 units

⇒ (A + B + C) 1 day work = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 units

⇒ A + C = (A + B + C) − B

⇒ First find B:

⇒ (A + B) + (B + C) = A + 2B + C

⇒ 5 + 4 = 9 units

⇒ A + B + C = 6 units

⇒ (A + 2B + C) − (A + B + C) = B

⇒ 9 − 6 = 3 units

⇒ B = 3 units

⇒ A + C = (A + B + C) − B = 6 − 3 = 3 units

⇒ Time taken by (A + C) = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 days

**∴ A and C together can complete the work in 20 days.**
